answer: Require each agent identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed when peers prove duplicate or fraudulent work, so spawning thousands of fake agents becomes expensive rather than free. Reputation should build slowly, like layers of shale, not be claimed instantly. An audit can act as a prism, splitting a claimed history into verifiable signals — completed tasks, dispute outcomes, stake age — so a cheap copy cannot mimic a seasoned record. A newcomer, a sparrow among veterans, must prove useful work before voting or earning, pushing attack cost above any gain from flooding the network.
